Replayed each 2026 deck charge from its 2026 start at the lower of 11.5 kW (Exhibit A of `civic_center_ev_service_agreement_draft.docx`) and that car's rating until its delivered energy, summing both decks per quarter-hour, except at the 101 pool-car hand-offs, where the attendant put a county pool car on a North Deck unit within ten minutes of another coming off (cars going on under 39 county permits in `ev_permit_registry.csv`; swaps noted on WO-26-0529 in `facilities_work_orders_2026.csv`): in every one the car ahead came off 6 to 20 minutes after finishing, while the decks' other charges stayed plugged in a median 6.7 hours after finishing, so the next car starts once the car ahead finishes at its new rate, after the same wait.

Took each month's highest quarter-hour beginning 12:00 to 19:45 on the billing days of `nspl_schedule_26_ev_charging_service.pdf` and grew it, unrounded, by the 1.12 in Table 1 of `fes-07_load_forecasting_standard_rev4.pdf` (one rounding, per its section 4): 97.4 kW at 12:00 on 21 January 2026 makes January 2028 109.1 kW, which files 110 kW in Schedule 26's 5 kW steps whether rounded to the nearest step or up.

Back-tested FES-07 on 2025 from the 2024 deck billing demand as its records stood when that forecast was made (FES-07 section 4, so the twelve 2024 sessions restated in March 2025 count at their earlier version), including `gateway_b_sessions_jan-apr2024.csv` and the fleet card charges in `fleet_card_ev_transactions_2024-2026.csv` the export does not carry (stamped in UTC, placed in local time), times the 1.08 factor in force then and rounded once, in whole kW against 2025's actual billing demand in whole kW, built the same way from the accepted 2025 versions in `restatement_decisions_2025.csv` with the January to March 2025 fleet card charges included: errors run from -1.9% to +2.5%, six over and six under.

Set each 2026 read span in `deck_panel_meter_log_2024-2026.xlsx`, its Corrections sheet applied, on the meters' standard-time clock (`deck_submeter_nameplates.csv`), the later 31 December South read standing, against the energy of the sessions on the units `deck_panel_circuit_schedule.csv` places on each panel, the weekend and holiday sessions in `curbline_courtesy_sessions_civic_decks_2024-2026.csv` included: 517 to 1,133 kWh unaccounted per read.
Recommendation: file 110 kW as the contracted demand for April 2027 to March 2028.

submission.objective_tag: Descriptive & Distribution Analysis (the distribution of time from filing to final decision for one fiscal year's applications, built from a docket-keyed production extract, with its median, lower quartile and 36-month share by technology group and the share still undecided).
steps: From `office_actions_FY2016_FY2026.parquet` took each docket's decision notice (its one NOA, REF or ABN action; GRT follows an allowance and decides nothing) and its first action on the merits (earliest EXR by `served_on`, then `action_id`), whose `credit_class` (1N or 1R) comes from `examiner_production_ledger_FY2016_FY2026.parquet` on `action_id`.

Read each CX edge in `docket_links.csv` by its successor's class: 1R is the same application re-examined after its refusal was set aside, and 1N is a continuing application filed on the successor's `docketed_on`, because the production standard credits 1N once per application, so a second 1N inside one CX chain would be a second application and the parent's refusal was never set aside (chaining every CX edge reads these successors as re-examinations); a benefit claim does not move the filing date (charter), and CN and DV children are applications of their own.

FY2022 applications are the dockets in `examination_dockets_FY2016_FY2026.parquet` with `docketed_on` from 1 October 2021 to 30 September 2022 that are not CX children, plus the CX children there whose first action on the merits is credited 1N: 66,186.

Final decision: from the application's docket follow each CX edge unless the successor's first action on the merits is credited 1N, and take the decision notice of the docket reached; where the next successor is credited 1N the decision is the refusal on the docket it leaves, a successor with no first action at the extract leaves the application waiting, and no notice by 30 September 2026 is still waiting at the extract (charter), so a docket's own notice or a transfer is never the end of a re-examined application: 10.6% undecided, none under 1,461 days.

Days from `docketed_on` to the final decision, Kaplan-Meier with the undecided censored at the extract, months as days over 30.4375 (charter), timing applications rather than the dockets Table P1 times: median 880 days, 28.9 months.

Recommendation: the headline prints 28.9 months.

submission.domain_tag: Physical & Environmental Sciences, environmental monitoring and exceedance (groundwater drawdown at landholder bores around an open-cut coal mine, attributed between climate and pumping).
submission.objective_tag: Anomaly Detection & Diagnostics (which bores show a decline the mine caused, as against the decline the dry seasons caused).
steps: Mapped every dip and logger to its bore through `landholder_bore_register.xlsx` (codes, registered numbers), converted the 2012 to 2014 EIS dips from feet, dropped entries keyed twice and dips whose remarks say the pump was running (MG-02 2.1), and reduced each dip to the measuring point in force on its date (MG-02 2.2).

Compensated each logger with `barometric_logger_2015-2026.csv` as the network notes set out, used the sensor depths in `logger_installations.csv`, and averaged the hours by Queensland day (MG-02 2.3).
Took each bore's September 2026 assessment level (MG-02 2.4) and its change since its baseline assessment in the register: the coal-measure bores near the pit fell only 2.21 to 2.49 m.

Fitted each bore's own gamma response to daily rainfall less a share of Morton areal evaporation (`daily_climate_1990-2026.csv`) on its readings to 3 July 2022: the coal-measure bores answer rain over six to seven years, the alluvium over about half a year.

Ran each fit forward to September 2026 and took the mine's drawdown as the fitted level less the assessment level: 8.2 to 9.3 m at the four coal-measure bores, 4.6 m at KV-LB12 and 2.4 m or less at the other 13.

Confirmed the fit on the three state reference bores, which it tracks within 0.3 m to September 2026, and with the take in `pit_dewatering_2022-2026.csv` fitted as a second stress over the full record: the same five bores.
Applied the triggers in MG-02 3.1 and the test in 4.1: KV-LB04, KV-LB05, KV-LB07, KV-LB10 and KV-LB12 have impaired capacity; the four complainants' bores do not.
Recommendation: four make-good offers under MG-02 6.1, with Yarrowmere's two bores in one agreement.

critical_components: The coal-measure bores KV-LB04, KV-LB05, KV-LB07 and KV-LB10 fell only **2.44, 2.49, 2.46 and 2.21 m** from their baseline assessments to September 2026

Each bore's own response to rainfall and evaporation, fitted before 4 July 2022 and run forward, puts the mine's drawdown at those four bores at **8.9, 9.3, 8.4 and 8.2 m**, and at KV-LB12 at **4.6 m**
The complainants' bores KV-LB01, KV-LB02, KV-LB06 and KV-LB18 fell **4.63, 5.23, 4.84 and 8.70 m**, of which the mine caused **0.8, 0.7, 0.6 and 1.3 m**
Five bores have impaired capacity, held by **four** owners
submission.recommendation: **Offer make-good agreements to four owners for five bores: Yarrowmere Pastoral Co Pty Ltd for KV-LB04 and KV-LB05 (one agreement), Tondara Grazing Pty Ltd for KV-LB07, Bluebush Downs Pty Ltd for KV-LB10 and Cypress Ridge Pastoral Trust for KV-LB12.** The mine's drawdown at the September 2026 level is 8.2 to 9.3 m at the four coal-measure bores against a 5 m trigger and 4.6 m at KV-LB12 against 2 m. Not the four complainants' bores: they fell, but through the dry seasons, and the mine's share is 0.6 to 1.3 m. Not the decline since the baseline assessment, which names the alluvial bores and the ridge bore and misses the coal measures, which were still rising on the 2019 to 2021 wet seasons when dewatering began. Not the decline less the reference bores' fall, which keeps KV-LB12 alone, because no reference bore is in the coal measures.
